markdown_report:
The strongest early-stage direction remains **candidate-conditioned recent-history attention added to SASRec**, tested as a small residual branch. Benefits remain hypotheses: the supplied inspiration’s 0.5600 score lacks a matched comparison establishing improvement.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already selects temporal evidence; another recency mechanism needs a control. (2) Candidate-specific recent evidence targets two observed failures: broad associations crowding out specific matches, and older incidental interactions outweighing recent repeated interests. It cannot establish compatibility or completed needs. (3) Electronics’ 14.95% negative-over-positive rate and −0.4812 lower-tail margin motivate discrimination experiments; modest embedding alignment does not establish collapse.

**Insights from related work.** (1) DIN establishes candidate-conditioned pooling; DARE motivates separate attention/value embeddings, reducing this proposal’s novelty. (2) FPMC/FOSSIL establish asymmetric transition scoring and lag-weighted aggregation; the pooling control is therefore substantive. (3) gSASRec motivates objective calibration as a simpler alternative. MARS motivates richer matching, but its pretrained-text evidence does not transfer directly.

The conceptual framework separates **evidence selection** (sequence attention, lag pooling, candidate attention, interest states), **representation** (shared IDs, independent tables, supplied text), and **supervision** (BCE, gBCE, sampled softmax). The first experiment changes selection and residual representation while retaining baseline supervision.

Scores are hypotheses. O/P/U/M denote originality, future potential, user-diagnosis alignment, and model-diagnosis alignment; D measures difficulty. Each cell gives an advantage and limitation.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-negative gBCE [gSASRec] | 2: focused / established | 7: reusable / sampling-sensitive | 3: discrimination / no intent selection | 8: confusion target / diagnostic transfer uncertain | 3: encoder retained / sampling cost |
| Recent candidate attention [DIN, DARE, FPMC] | 3: targeted combination / established mechanisms | 6: extensible / sparse evidence | 7: specificity and recency / no compatibility labels | 6: discrimination / bounded influence | 6: short window / scorer and budget complexity |
| Three causal interest states [D2MFRec] | 4: persistence / established routing | 7: richer history / unstable states | 7: recurring interests / completion unobserved | 5: differentiated features / indirect link | 7: compact / causal routing complexity |

Select recent candidate attention at 0% progress for explicit diagnosis alignment and a bounded implementation. Attend over the last ten valid events using independent attention and directional value tables. Compare baseline, exponential pooling, and candidate attention with identical value/target heads; report additional active attention parameters rather than adding unused parameters to claim capacity parity.

Retain fixed α=0.1 initially: because the cosine residual lies in [−1,1], it can change a fixed-backbone pairwise gap by at most 0.2. Record score scale and ranking flips; do not claim this bounds jointly trained model differences. Learned gains remain future work.

Select exclusively by pinned sampled macro validation HR@10. Report every configuration, category results, conditional paired uncertainty when available, and selection optimism. Sampled improvements do not establish full-catalog or satisfaction gains.

idea.description: Add a bounded candidate-conditioned attention residual over the ten most recent valid prefix interactions to each dataset’s SASRec model. Use an attention embedding table separate from directional source-value and candidate-target tables, retaining the baseline encoder and objective. Treat this as an incremental combination of DIN-style candidate selection, DARE-style embedding separation, and FPMC/FOSSIL-style transition scoring.
idea.motivation: The branch explicitly targets two user-facing failures: broadly associated items displacing specific matches, and older incidental interactions outweighing recent repeated evidence. Candidate-conditioned weights select supporting events separately for each recommendation; a recent window and decay constrain old evidence, and repeated occurrences contribute separately. These mechanisms do not identify semantic intent, compatibility, usefulness, or completed needs. The model-facing target is weak positive–negative discrimination, especially Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative tenth-percentile margin. Multi-negative gBCE remains a strong simpler alternative, but it lacks an explicit mechanism for the two selected user-facing failures. No improvement is established before the pinned evaluation.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve all four original datasets and routing, input splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Save all artifacts beneath the trial directory and execute each trial on one GPU. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS, default 200. Use no external weights, hidden test data, unavailable reviews, ratings, item categories, prices, stores, compatibility labels, or simulator traits. Titles, descriptions, and public training timestamps remain permitted but unused in the initial ID-only experiment.

Retain the actual RecHarness sasrec_perdataset encoder, optimizer, sampler, batch size, loss reduction, and existing regularization. Record their resolved settings in each artifact manifest rather than substituting generic SASRec defaults. Add branch parameters to the same optimizer with its existing learning rate and optimizer options; apply no additional branch-specific regularization in this initial experiment, and record that choice. Retain the sampler’s existing exclusions without reading validation or test labels to construct exclusions. Document its behavior because unobserved samples are not verified negatives. Do not introduce hard-negative mining, new clipping, normalization of baseline logits, or a changed loss in this comparison.

Use K=10 recent valid events, branch dimension d=16, decay=0.8, attention temperature 0.2, and fixed alpha=0.1. These are frozen engineering choices, not literature-established optima. Construct independent attention table A, source-value table V, and candidate-target table T, each with padding index zero. A supplies both history keys and candidate queries; it is separate from V and T, rather than separate query and key tables. Initialize nonpadding entries independently from Normal(0, 0.02), set padding rows to zero, and use F.normalize(..., p=2, dim=-1, eps=1e-6). Initialize all tables with nonzero norms. Apply no branch dropout.

For each prefix position, gather the most recent K nonpadding events in newest-first order, including the current prefix item, with event lags 0 through K-1. Padding does not consume an event lag. Keep repeated occurrences as separate events; do not deduplicate them. For candidate j, attention logits are cosine(A[item], A[j])/0.2 + lag*log(0.8). Normalize over valid history events separately for each candidate. Values are cosine(V[item], T[j]), and the residual is their attention-weighted sum. Mask padding explicitly after transformations. Use a safe masked softmax returning all-zero weights for an empty history; never softmax an all-negative-infinity row. Exclude padded positive targets from loss and prevent item zero from being recommended. Causal gathering must not use targets or future events.

The combined score is baseline_logit + 0.1*residual. Since the residual lies in [-1,1], its direct effect on a pairwise gap is at most 0.2 when baseline features and weights are held fixed. This may be too small relative to unnormalized SASRec scores. It does not bound differences between independently optimized configurations, since the residual also changes encoder gradients. Prespecify the fixed coefficient to avoid an additional search dimension; do not tune it after inspecting validation scores. Learned positive per-dataset gains or gains scaled by a detached training-logit spread are future alternatives, not extra configurations in this experiment. Multiplying the complete score by a positive constant cannot improve its ranking.

Prespecify exactly three configurations in this order: unchanged SASRec; SASRec plus candidate-independent exponential pooling using the same V/T scoring head; and SASRec plus candidate attention. The pooling weights are proportional to 0.8^lag over valid events. Both residual configurations use identical K, d, alpha, V/T initialization, optimizer treatment, and causal gathering. Initialize V/T before A so corresponding V/T draws agree across the two residual configurations. Construct branches after baseline initialization within torch.random.fork_rng, including CUDA devices if initialization draws there, to preserve the baseline’s subsequent random stream. The branch has no stochastic forward operations. This preserves initialization streams, not identical optimization trajectories.

Do not register unused A parameters in the pooling control. Report active parameter counts and measured compute: candidate attention adds (number_of_items+1)*16 parameters beyond pooling, so this comparison cannot isolate conditioning from added attention capacity. The shared V/T head controls directional transition capacity. A future actively trained capacity-matched control, tied versus decoupled tables, projection-based versus independent embeddings, smaller attention dimensions, last-item/uniform/learned-lag pooling, residual-only scoring, window-size comparisons, and within-window shuffling would further separate mechanisms. These are documented limitations and future controls, not additional searches under this schedule.

Allocate at most 12,000 GPU-seconds per configuration across all four datasets, reserving 7,200 seconds for diagnostics, debugging, and failures. These caps total 43,200 seconds only if the full shared budget remains; subtract all earlier training, diagnostics, failures, and adaptive trials first. If less remains, proportionally reduce the three configuration allocations and reserve before starting, record the resulting plan, and avoid claiming that previous exploration was free. Count timing pilots and checkpoint restoration against the appropriate allocation.

Use charged baseline timing to freeze a common epoch cap no greater than the environment limit, then train every configuration/category to that cap. Do not select checkpoints by intermediate validation performance. If an allocation cannot complete the cap, compare only a previously saved epoch completed by all twelve configuration/category combinations; otherwise the comparison is incomplete. Save epoch checkpoints inside the trial directory to make this fallback possible, subject to storage constraints. Do not compare different epoch counts under a claimed common-epoch protocol. Record actual GPU time, throughput, epochs, and all evaluated checkpoints. The 12,000-second caps are ceilings, not evidence that 200 epochs will fit.

Select by the largest unrounded host-provided equal-weight macro validation HR@10; prefer baseline on ties, then the listed configuration order. Retain the pinned 200 validation users per dataset, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42. Do not change or reimplement the evaluator. Report all three configurations, all four dataset scores, macro differences, and the full search history. One changed hit moves dataset HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Fixed unique negatives improve reproducibility without removing sampled-metric bias. Describe gains specifically as pinned sampled-validation improvements, not full-catalog improvements.

If the existing host outputs expose paired per-user hits on identical candidates, perform 10,000 paired dataset-stratified bootstrap replicates with a separate NumPy default_rng(42). In each replicate, independently resample 200 user indices with replacement within each dataset, reuse those indices across configurations, calculate each dataset’s HR difference, and average the four differences equally. Report percentile 95% intervals and baseline-only versus variant-only hits. These intervals condition on trained models, fixed candidates, and these datasets; they exclude training-seed variation, negative-resampling variation, other-dataset uncertainty, and selection adjustment. Sparse disagreements can make intervals unstable. Selecting the best configuration on this validation set creates winner’s-curse optimism; ordinary post-selection bootstrap intervals do not correct it. If host outputs do not expose the required paired outcomes, state that the analysis is unavailable. Reserve independent held-out assessment for the host’s final evaluation.

Candidate dependence requires explicit compatibility adapters. log2feats returns a feature container holding encoder features and causal recent-item context. predict_score accepts that container and dispatches by explicit feature rank: B x L x H encoder features with B x L items means aligned training scoring; B x H encoder features with B x C items means candidate-set scoring. Do not infer these modes merely from equal dimension lengths. Provide a last_position helper that selects both encoder features and matching recent context. Update diagnosis code that previously indexed tensor features directly. Retain view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, view.item_emb as the base table, and user_train, meta_data, review_data. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; train_loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B x L tensors.

Compute margins with the complete scorer. Label embedding cosine diagnostics as measurements of the base item table, not the entire candidate-dependent model. Mark item-category breakdowns unavailable; dataset names do not supply item-level category metadata. Use deterministic bounded public-history diagnostic samples and report sample counts. Where existing permitted validation outputs expose scores, record baseline logit spread, rank-10/11 gaps, positive-to-cutoff gaps, residual differences, and ranking flips without altering evaluation or using these diagnostics for tuning. Otherwise label equivalent measurements on training-prefix candidate sets as training diagnostics. Define the cutoff as the tenth-highest score among the 99 negatives when measuring a positive’s gap to the hit threshold. Report tie handling and do not reinterpret training diagnostics as validation results.

Diagnose shortcut learning using counts computed only from training histories: training target frequency, and whether each recent-source-to-target pair previously appeared as an adjacent transition. Report complete-score margins and residual magnitude separately for seen and unseen transition support, plus target-frequency groups using documented training-count quartiles. Count repeated adjacent transitions consistently. Use these as descriptive analyses, with group sample sizes; a seen-transition advantage alone does not establish harmful memorization. Candidate attention may exploit popular transitions, item identity, repeated purchases, and accidental co-occurrence. A recent window may suppress useful persistent interests, while separate tables can overfit sparse items. No compatibility, semantic precision, or need-completion claim follows from these mechanisms.

Update the predictor writer to serialize architecture version, baseline settings, all branch hyperparameters, normalization epsilon, initialization specification, state dictionaries, item mappings, and dataset routing. Reconstruct precisely the training scorer in working/predict.py and set eval mode for inference. Candidate scoring costs O(B*C*K*d) for the branch, so chunk full-catalog candidates for recommendations to the twenty designated real training users, five per dataset. Normalize attention over history independently for every candidate so chunk size cannot affect scores. Exclude known training items for these unseen-item lists using the established simulator contract; retain the host’s own candidate handling for benchmark evaluation.

Verify save/reload score agreement with atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5, causal invariance to future suffix changes, masked-history padding invariance, candidate-order equivariance, finite empty-history outputs, aligned-versus-single-candidate agreement, and chunked-versus-unchunked agreement. Padding checks must preserve the baseline’s original positional indexing; do not claim that arbitrary position shifts leave learned positional embeddings invariant. Check the branch’s fixed-backbone pairwise perturbation bound with numerical tolerance. These public-history checks and diagnostics consume the search budget. Simulator feedback remains descriptive and must not trigger additional tuning. Report observed outcomes and limitations without inventing validation gains or asserting compatibility, satisfaction, or full-catalog improvement.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIGS = [baseline, exponential_pooling, candidate_attention]
K, D, DECAY, TAU, ALPHA, EPS = 10, 16, 0.8, 0.2, 0.1, 1e-6

class Features:
    h            # B,L,H for aligned training; B,H for candidate evaluation
    recent_ids   # B,L,K or B,K, newest first
    lags         # corresponding valid-event lags
    mask         # corresponding valid-history mask

class RecentCandidateSASRec(nn.Module):
    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        h = self.baseline.log2feats(sequence)
        ids, lags, mask = causal_last_k_valid_events(sequence, K)
        return Features(h, ids, lags, mask)

    def last_position(self, features):
        return select_matching_final_position_from_all_fields(features)

    def score_contexts(self, features, candidates):
        # Flattened contexts: h=N,H; ids=N,K; candidates=N,C.
        base = einsum('nh,nch->nc', features.h, self.item_emb(candidates))
        values = normalize(self.V(features.recent_ids), eps=EPS)
        targets = normalize(self.T(candidates), eps=EPS)
        transitions = einsum('nkd,ncd->nck', values, targets)
        logits = features.lags[:, None, :] * log(DECAY)
        if self.mode == 'candidate_attention':
            keys = normalize(self.A(features.recent_ids), eps=EPS)
            queries = normalize(self.A(candidates), eps=EPS)
            logits = logits + einsum('nkd,ncd->nck', keys, queries) / TAU
        logits = broadcast_to_candidate_count(logits, candidates.shape[1])
        weights = safe_masked_softmax(logits, features.mask[:, None, :])
        residual = (weights * transitions).sum(-1)
        return base + ALPHA * residual

    def predict_score(self, features, items):
        if features.h.ndim == 3:
            assert items.shape == features.h.shape[:2]
            flat = flatten_batch_and_time(features)
            scores = self.score_contexts(flat, items.reshape(-1, 1))
            return scores.reshape(items.shape)
        assert features.h.ndim == 2 and items.ndim == 2
        assert features.h.shape[0] == items.shape[0]
        return self.score_contexts(features, items)

remaining_budget = 43200 - all_previously_charged_GPU_seconds
freeze_and_log_allocations(remaining_budget, ratio=[12000,12000,12000,7200])
common_epoch_cap = charged_baseline_timing_plan(max_epochs=env_SASREC_EPOCHS_default_200)

for configuration in CONFIGS:
    for dataset in ORIGINAL_FOUR_DATASETS:
        seed_training(42)
        model = construct_actual_recharness_sasrec_perdataset(dataset)
        if configuration != baseline:
            with fork_rng_preserving_baseline_streams():
                initialize_V_then_T_normal_std_002(model, D)
                if configuration == candidate_attention:
                    initialize_A_normal_std_002(model, D)
            attach_branch_and_explicit_optimizer_parameters(model, configuration)
        train_with_unchanged_sampler_loss_and_optimizer(model, common_epoch_cap)
        save_epoch_states_configuration_and_routing_under_trial_directory(model)
    write_predictor_reconstructing_identical_architecture_and_scoring()
    run_public_history_consistency_checks_with_charged_cost()
    record_existing_host_validation_outputs_and_all_GPU_seconds()

require_same_completed_epoch_for_all_configurations_and_datasets()
report_every_configuration_and_per_dataset_HR10()
select_highest_unrounded_host_macro_HR10_with_prespecified_ties()
if existing_host_has_paired_user_hits:
    paired_dataset_stratified_bootstrap(replicates=10000, numpy_seed=42)
run_compatible_diagnostics_and_descriptive_simulator_without_further_tuning()

originality.positive: The constrained combination targets two concrete user failures and tests candidate selection against the same directional transition head.
originality.negative: DIN establishes candidate-conditioned pooling, DARE separates attention and representation embeddings, and FPMC/FOSSIL establish asymmetric transition scoring; neither component nor their broad combination is a new model family.

future_potential.positive: A short candidate-conditioned branch offers a tractable foundation for studying supported recommendations, scale calibration, and later use of supplied titles and descriptions.
future_potential.negative: Sparse-table overfitting, transition shortcuts, uncertain residual scale, and the absence of compatibility or completion labels limit likely generality.

code_difficulty.positive: The baseline encoder and objective remain intact, and the branch uses small tables and a fixed ten-event window.
code_difficulty.negative: Structured causal features, explicit aligned/candidate scoring, full-catalog chunking, predictor and diagnosis synchronization, and strict shared-budget accounting make this more involved than a simple additive head.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention over interaction histories for next-item prediction.
The original implementation scores with unnormalized dot products, making residual scale consequential.
limitations: Already models temporal evidence selection, so additional recency mechanisms require controls.
Interaction prediction does not identify equipment compatibility, completed needs, or satisfaction.

related_work.title: MARS
contributions: Motivates attribute-aware text representations and user–candidate matching across multiple preference signals.
limitations: Its pretrained-language-model setting cannot be imported into this task.
Does not establish effectiveness of the proposed ID-only residual.

related_work.title: DARE
contributions: Separates attention embeddings from history representation embeddings to reduce gradient interference.
Studies smaller attention dimensions, providing precedent for a compact attention table.
limitations: Evidence concerns long-history CTR prediction rather than this sparse next-item benchmark.
Independent tables add parameters and can overfit sparse items; projections were not equivalent remedies in its experiments.

related_work.title: gSASRec: sampled-loss calibration for sequential recommendation
contributions: Studies overconfidence from sampled BCE and proposes gBCE with increased negative sampling.
limitations: Does not directly select recent candidate-specific evidence.
Reported improvements do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluator.

related_work.title: D2MFRec
contributions: Combines soft-clustered interest representations and sequential representations through learned gates.
limitations: Interest differentiation does not identify completed needs.
Additional routing and state modeling increase implementation and search costs.

related_work.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
contributions: Conditions history aggregation on each candidate through a local activation mechanism.
Introduces mini-batch-aware regularization relevant to sparse embedding features.
limitations: Establishes substantial prior art for the proposal’s candidate-conditioned pooling.
Its CTR setting and regularization results do not establish transfer to this benchmark.

related_work.title: Factorizing Personalized Markov Chains for Next-Basket Recommendation
contributions: Combines personalized preference scoring with directional source–target transition factors.
limitations: Establishes prior art for separate source and target transition tables.
Transition likelihood alone cannot distinguish useful complements from duplicate or completed purchases.

related_work.title: FOSSIL: FactOrized Sequential prediction with Item SImilarity ModeLs
contributions: Combines history-based similarity with higher-order transitions and global/user-specific lag weights.
Uses parameter sharing to address sparse interaction data.
limitations: Its lag pooling is candidate-independent, leaving candidate-specific event selection as a distinct experimental question.
Does not establish the benefit of independent residual tables on sparse Amazon histories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model ordering.
limitations: Does not invalidate the required pinned benchmark, but limits conclusions to its sampled evaluation protocol.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling that preserves correspondence between observations.
Supports the proposed within-dataset paired user bootstrap.
limitations: A stratified macro calculation must be implemented explicitly.
Ordinary bootstrap intervals do not capture training-seed variability or automatically adjust for model selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection-induced optimism from optimizing models against finite validation data.
limitations: Reporting conditional intervals and limiting configurations do not eliminate selection bias; independent assessment remains necessary.

related_work.title: HLLM SASRec implementation
contributions: Provides implementation precedent for normalized representations and explicit cosine-logit scaling.
limitations: Does not establish that alpha=0.1 is appropriate for a bounded residual added to unnormalized SASRec logits.
An unpinned implementation is contextual evidence rather than this experiment’s reproducibility specification.

related_work.title: ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Provides precedent for zero-initialized residual gates.
limitations: A zero gate initially blocks gradients to branch parameters.
Does not justify zero-initializing normalized branch vectors or establish an appropriate recommendation-score scale.
